title: Don't Throw The Book At Them

contact_edits.before: After all of which, it's awkward to have to admit that the show is always involving and ultimately moving. Credit goes to the history, to the music and to the fact that the creators, however much they fumble, do seem genuinely involved with the subject. The cast helps, too: Richard Harte, Brandon McGibbon, Tracy Dawson and Jacquelyn French give pungent if oddly uneasy accounts of team players and team fans, while Richard McMillan as priestly team coach takes some stock jokes and good intentions and makes a man of them. But it's John and Mary who really lump our throats by letting us partake in their growing up. Tony LePage is lithe, sympathetic and, when bitterness is called for, powerful. Peck is superb, confirming what she promised in We Will Rock You: that she's a first-rate theatre singer who's also a charming and economical actress, forceful without forcing and capable of projecting a passionate moral strength. It's a strangely admirable show. Let me put it like this: It's often dumb, but it's not stupid. - The Boys in the Photograph is at the Royal Alexandra Theatre until Nov. 1. For tickets and information call 416-872-1212 or visit mirvish.com.
